food_name: Beneforté broccoli, sulforaphane yield after analytical myrosinase hydrolysis (raw sample)
food_database: Abukhabta et al. 2021, European Journal of Nutrition, Figure 1
food_part: Whole broccoli head, 4–5 cm from top; heads combined thoroughly
geographical_origin: Supplier Staples Vegetables Ltd., Boston, Lincolnshire, UK
synonym_verification_status: Sulforaphane separately quantified against sulforaphane external standard
synonym_source: Abukhabta et al. 2021; GC–MS, external sulforaphane standard
mapping_review_rationale: Manual exact identity mapping: source analyte sulforaphane and Stage B target match by PubChem CID and full InChIKey from the Stage B snapshot/PubChem. The source uses an external sulforaphane standard. Stage B was not edited.
moisture_basis: Dry weight of lyophilized broccoli powder; fresh broccoli solids content 11.9% reported, but no fresh-weight conversion made
extraction_method: Lyophilized powder (0.5 g) incubated in 10 mL deionized water for 1 h at 30 °C to hydrolyze glucosinolates via myrosinase; dichloromethane extraction
sample_size: Not clearly stated for Figure 1 concentration assay; figure shows error bars. Do not assume n=3 from triplicate antibacterial tests.
source_title: Sulforaphane-enriched extracts from glucoraphanin-rich broccoli exert antimicrobial activity against gut pathogens and innovative cooking methods increase in vivo intestinal delivery of sulforaphane
database_reference: Figure 1/results: 0.57 or 0.58 µmol/g DW after standardized myrosinase hydrolysis; converted with MW 177.29 g/mol to mg/kg DW
extraction_notes: Reported 0.57 µmol/g dry weight. Converted to 101.0553 mg/kg dry weight using MW 177.29 g/mol: µmol/g × 177.29 = mg/kg. This is sulforaphane recovered after analytical water incubation designed to hydrolyze glucosinolates, not a direct measurement of pre-existing unhydrolyzed free sulforaphane in the intact food. Accepted only as an operational hydrolysis-released sulforaphane yield from broccoli material. The source reports 0.57/0.58 µmol/g DW after 1 h water incubation at 30°C with myrosinase hydrolysis; converted using 177.29 g/mol to 101.0553/102.8282 mg/kg DW.
uncertainty_notes: Beneforté is a glucoraphanin-rich experimental cultivar and may differ from ordinary retail broccoli. Concentration is hydrolysis-dependent, dry-weight basis; reporting/replicate count for Figure 1 not clear in accessible methods. Hold as candidate until exposure interpretation accepts analytical generation as food-relevant sulforaphane potential. NOT a direct measure of pre-existing free sulforaphane in intact broccoli. Analytical hydrolysis creates/releases analyte from glucosinolates. Experimental Beneforté cultivar, lyophilized dry-weight basis; concentration-assay replicate/statistical unit is unclear.
